name: Xiangsha Liujunzi decoction
short: Sparse data from poor-quality trials: a review of dyspepsia trials found no adverse events reported in the groups given the formula; other reviews give no event details.
text: Safety reporting for Xiangsha Liujunzi decoction comes from reviews of low-quality trials. A 2012 meta-analysis of 15 publications of randomized trials of Liu Jun Zi Tang and Xiangsha Liujunzi Tang for functional dyspepsia, whose reported comparisons were with prokinetic drugs, states that no adverse events were reported in the groups given either formula in any of the included trials; the abstract does not say how many trials assessed adverse events, and the authors note poor methodological quality in most of them. A 2024 meta-analysis of 23 trials (2,101 people) in functional dyspepsia found no significant difference in safety between the decoction and control groups (risk ratio 0.67, 95% CI 0.16 to 2.76), and its abstract gives no event counts. A 2014 review of 10 trials of the decoction or a modified version in diabetic gastroparesis states only that two trials recorded adverse events, without saying what they were. The abstracts do not list the herbs in the formula. No interaction data were found in the cited sources.
